metadata.title: Eclipsing binaries at the conjunctions predicted by near-edge-on Gaia DR3 astrometric orbits: data, predictions and code
metadata.description:
Data, code and predictions for the Research Note of the AAS "Eclipsing binaries at the conjunctions predicted by near-edge-on Gaia DR3 astrometric orbits" (Chopard-Vilhem 2026).

Unlike spectroscopic orbits, Gaia DR3 astrometric orbits give the inclination, and an orbit seen edge-on predicts when its eclipses occur. The 1726 astrometric orbits brighter than G = 14 whose best-fitting inclination lies within 1° of 90° were selected, their uncertainties propagated to the times of the two conjunctions, and the TESS light curves (SPOC, TESS-SPOC, QLP) searched at those times. Seven new eclipsing binaries, with periods of 26 to 242 days, show eclipses at the predicted times, with false-alarm probabilities below 3×10−5.

Contents

  • the selection of 1726 orbits and their Gaia DR3 orbital elements;
  • every search window and flag, all single events, and the false-alarm trials;
  • the face-on control: the same search on 2000 orbits that cannot eclipse;
  • the artefact vetting and its calibration on 256 known eclipses;
  • the injection–recovery tests and the bounds on compact companions;
  • pixel-level difference images and literature checks of the candidates;
  • predicted times of the next eclipses with their uncertainties (October 2026 to June 2028), and a calendar of those observable from Cluj-Napoca;
  • the figure of the note and all the code.

Version 1.2.0 is the version cited by the note. It corrects version 1.1.0: one of the seven systems, CD−81 705, also has a QLP flag and holds without it; the figure and the calibration of the Gaia timing uncertainties leave out the two withdrawn systems, after which the eclipse times scatter more than the propagated uncertainties; counts refer to distinct dips. Version 1.1.0 added the face-on control, which shows a false-alarm rate of 23 per cent for QLP windows and none for SPOC and TESS-SPOC windows. See the README for details.

Reproducibility. Every number quoted in the note is recomputed from these files by code/n2_statistics.py into n2_numbers.txt ("N2" is the working name of the note); this was reproduced identically on a second machine. See README.md for the contents of each file and notes for re-use.

Testing the predictions. predictions/eclipse_predictions.csv gives the mid-eclipse times (UTC), their 1σ uncertainties, depths and durations. Only eclipses after the publication date of version 1.0.0 (13 October 2026) are genuine forecasts. Observations that confirm or refute them are welcome: t.chopard.research@proton.me.
